title: Karnataka: 'Bandh' called in three Chikkaballapur taluks over denial of cabinet berth to Bagepalli MLA SN Subbareddy - India's News.Net
full_text:
Chikkaballapur (Karnataka) [India], August 5 (ANI): A 'bandh' has been called on Wednesday by the supporters of Congress MLA SN Subbareddy in three taluks of Chikkaballapur district to protest his exclusion from the newly expanded Karnataka cabinet.
Subbareddy is the Congress MLA from Bagepalli assembly constituency.
Congress workers and Subbareddy's supporters have taken to the streets in Bagepalli, Gudibande and Chelur taluks, urging traders to voluntarily shut their shops. Commercial activities were affected in several places due to the 'bandh'.
The protesters said that Subbareddy, a senior leader and elected representative of the constituency, deserved a place in the cabinet. They urged the Congress high command and the state leadership to reconsider the decision and induct him into the cabinet.
In view of the bandh, tight police security has been deployed across the three taluks, with precautionary measures taken to prevent any untoward incidents.
The district administration and the police are closely monitoring the situation and the developments related to the bandh.
Earlier on Tuesday, Congress leader Gayathri Shanthegowda reacted with restraint after her name was reportedly included in the initial list for the Karnataka cabinet expansion but removed in a revised list released minutes later.
'I'm a loyal party worker. I don't want to react now; I've already said I'm an honest party worker. I came from the grassroots level, and I will follow whatever the party says,' Shanthegowda told ANI.
Her name was dropped during the finalisation of the cabinet under the DK Shivakumar government.
Shanthegowda was notably the only woman leader whose name appeared in the first list of prospective ministers. However, in a swift turn of events, a second list was released just minutes later, in which her name was absent.
Several senior Congress leaders, including HK Patil, Dinesh Gundu Rao, Lakshmi Hebbalkar, Shivanand Patil, RB Thimmapur, RV Deshpande, K Venkatesh, Krishnappa, Tanveer Sait, Appaji Nadagouda and HC Mahadevappa, were left out of the expanded cabinet.
Many of them have previously served as ministers in Congress governments and were considered strong contenders for cabinet positions. Their exclusion has triggered discussions within the party over the balance between seniority, regional representation and community considerations in the allocation of portfolios.
The expansion of the Karnataka cabinet has triggered discontent among several senior Congress leaders who were left out. (ANI)

title: Japan unveils human refrigerator to beat extreme heat - Dailyhunt
full_text:
Tokyo: As record-breaking summer temperatures continue to grip Japan, the country has introduced an innovative cooling solution a human-sized refrigerator designed to help people recover quickly from heat exhaustion and prevent heatstroke.
Called the Do Hiemon Box, the one-person cooling booth is already being deployed at construction sites, factories, universities and public facilities as Japan battles increasingly severe heatwaves.
Developed by Japanese refrigeration manufacturer SDRS and marketed by industrial equipment supplier Trusco Nakayama, the booth has attracted attention worldwide for its unusual yet practical approach to protecting people from extreme heat.
A refrigerator designed for people
Unlike a conventional refrigerator, the Do Hiemon Box is specifically designed to cool the human body rapidly.
The stainless-steel booth, roughly the size of a vending machine, contains a built-in seat where a person can sit while chilled air is directed towards the head, neck, shoulders and back. Once the glass door is closed, the interior remains at around 15°C, while 5°C air is blown onto the user to provide quick relief from high temperatures.
Built to prevent heatstroke
According to the manufacturers, users begin to feel noticeably cooler within about five minutes, while spending around 10 minutes inside can help reduce symptoms of heat exhaustion.
The system automatically switches off after 20 minutes to prevent overcooling and offers multiple airflow settings depending on the user’s needs. Rather than serving as a place to relax, the booth has been designed as emergency cooling equipment for people exposed to intense heat.
Designed for workplaces and public spaces
The Do Hiemon Box is primarily intended for locations where people spend long hours working outdoors or in high-temperature environments.
Construction sites, steel plants, warehouses, factories, golf courses, universities and outdoor event venues are among the first facilities to adopt the cooling booths. The unit runs on a standard electrical connection, requires no permanent installation and is mounted on wheels for easy movement.
Japan’s extreme heat drives innovation
Japan has been experiencing increasingly intense summers, with temperatures regularly crossing 35°C and heatstroke cases rising sharply.
The country’s weather agency has introduced new terminology for exceptionally hot days, while authorities routinely issue heatstroke warnings during summer. Rising temperatures have prompted businesses to develop innovative cooling technologies to protect workers and the public.
Demand growing at home and abroad
Trusco Nakayama has already sold around 200 units of the Do Hiemon Box since its launch earlier this year.
The company says it has received enquiries from overseas, including Germany and the United States, as governments and businesses explore new ways to cope with increasingly frequent heatwaves. A standard unit costs approximately 1.5 million yen (around USD 9,500), making it primarily suitable for organisations rather than individual consumers.
Could become more common
With climate change contributing to hotter summers across many parts of the world, the company believes such cooling booths could eventually become common in shopping malls, transport hubs, workplaces and public spaces.
As governments strengthen workplace safety rules related to heat exposure, demand for rapid body-cooling systems is expected to increase further.
Conclusion
Japan’s Do Hiemon Box represents an innovative response to rising global temperatures, offering people a quick way to cool down and reduce the risk of heat-related illnesses. While currently aimed at businesses and public institutions, the human-sized refrigerator reflects how countries are increasingly turning to technology to adapt to the growing challenge of extreme heat.
